CONFIRM C0188 — near-duplicate feedback is order-dependent. The current artifact still handles only `fid_a`, so `(prior_id, current_id, sim)` silently drops feedback when `prior_id` is absent from current-round `findings`.

FINDING_ID: C0188_REFORMAT_FIX
SEVERITY: 0.75
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.30
FIND: C0188 is confirmed by the current source. In `bench/dm/_feedback.py`, `build_feedback_records()` documents `duplicate_pairs` as generic `(finding_id_a, finding_id_b, similarity)` pairs, but the implementation only looks up `fid_a` in `finding_by_id` and appends duplicate feedback to `fid_a`. If the similarity stage emits `(OLD7, NEW1, 0.93)` and only `NEW1` is in the current `findings`, `finding_by_id.get("OLD7")` returns `None`, the loop continues, and `NEW1` receives no feedback.
FOLLOW: The similarity stage can identify a current finding as a near-duplicate of a prior finding, but this function is the sole renderer bridge into §17 feedback. If pair ordering is prior/current rather than current/prior, `_render_single_record()` never receives `rec.duplicates`, so the model is not instructed to differentiate or withdraw. This weakens duplicate suppression and pollutes convergence with preventable repeated claims.
ANALYSE: HARD relative to the documented interface. Premises: (1) the docstring does not require `fid_a` to be the current-round finding; (2) prior findings may not appear in current-round `findings`; (3) the implementation checks only `fid_a`; (4) feedback should be sent to the current finding if either side of the pair is current. Concrete trace: `findings=[NEW1(model_id="M1")]`, `duplicate_pairs=[("OLD7","NEW1",0.93)]`; current code skips because `OLD7` is absent and never considers `NEW1`. Conclusion: CONFIRMED.
